messages:
peter: Heads up — customer hit AccessDenied when decrypting after region failover. They use AWS multi-region keys (MRKs) + cross-account role. Anyone seen this? :eyes:

hema: Can you paste the decrypt error and the principal ARN they were calling with?

peter: Here’s the error from the app logs:
```json
{
  "error": "AccessDeniedException",
  "message": "User: arn:aws:sts::333444555:assumed-role/thirdparty-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111222333:key/replica-key-id"
}
```

hema: Two quick things to verify: 1) are they attempting decrypt using the replica key ARN (region-specific) or the primary key ARN? 2) check the replica key policy — MRKs do not implicitly copy cross-account IAM grants/policies to replicas.

ida: We ran into this same class of failure last quarter. TL;DR: grants are regional and people often assume key policy replication covers external principals. Short fix is to create an explicit grant in the replica region for the external principal, or update the replica key policy to allow that principal.

ida: Example key policy snippet (minimal):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::333444555:role/thirdparty-role" },
      "Action": "kms:Decrypt",
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

hema: Also check CloudTrail for kms:Decrypt events in both regions to confirm which key ARN the request hit and whether there are any EncryptionContext mismatches. CloudTrail will show the principal that made the call and the key ARN used.

infra-bot: added CloudTrail query link for the account/region: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail/home?region=eu-west-1#events:queryId=REDACTED

sec-oncall: Short-term mitigation: either route decrypt calls to the primary region (if acceptable) or create the cross-account grant in the replica region. For long-term, add an onboarding check that validates MRK replicas contain the expected principals/grants after any rotation.

peter: I’ll try creating the grant in the replica region and replay the failing request. Will report back with logs. Thanks folks! :thumbsup:

hema: If the grant doesn't fix it, double-check rotation history and any code that pins raw key ARNs (rotation can change identifiers clients rely on). Also confirm the app is not sending a ciphertext blob tied to a different region's key.

peter: noted — will follow up by EOD.
